We develop UNICASE for the Eclipse platform with the Eclipse Java IDE.

We currently use the following development tools:

    * Java 5 SE
    * Eclipse 3.4: Modeling Tools Edition (Ganymede)
          o EMF
          o GEF, GMF
          o Ecore Tools

    * Eclipse Plugins
          o UNICASE: install via Update Manager - http://wwwbruegge.in.tum.de/static/unicase
          o COPE: install via Update Manager - http://cope.in.tum.de/update-site/site.xml
          o Subclipse: install via Update Manager - http://subclipse.tigris.org/update_1.4.x
          o Checkstyle: install via Update Manager (use version 4.x) - http://eclipse-cs.sourceforge.net/update
          o Findbugs: install via Update Manager - http://findbugs.cs.umd.edu/eclipse


Getting started as developer in 7 easy steps:

1. Download and install Java.

2. Download Eclipse and install the required plugins (see above).

3. Checkout the UNICASE source code from the svn repository (see this link: http://code.google.com/p/unicase/source/checkout).

4. Configure Java and Checkstyle warnings as described in Coding Guidelines.

5. Start the UNICASE server from Eclipse, see this video tutorial.

6. Start the UNICASE client from Eclipse, see this video tutorial.

7. Register for our mailinglists.


If you have any questions please consider the FAQ and Developer FAQ and do not hesitate to use our mailinglist.

Note: We use UNICASE to model unicase, also called boot strapping or eat-your-own-dogfood.See here: http://code.google.com/p/unicase/wiki/Unicase_repository_beta_server   for details.
